categories.nameJa: サーキュラーエコノミー

entries.factEn: Without the natural greenhouse effect, Earth's average temperature would be about -18C instead of the current 15C. Human activity has increased atmospheric CO2 by over 50% since pre-industrial times.
entries.hintEn: Save 2 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Oceans absorb about 30% of human-produced CO2 and forests absorb another 30%. Together these natural carbon sinks remove roughly 9.5 billion tonnes of CO2 from the atmosphere each year.
entries.hintEn: Save 5 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Standby and idle power consumption accounts for 5-10% of residential electricity use. Using smart power strips to fully cut power to entertainment systems, chargers, and idle electronics can save 100+ kg of CO2 per household per year.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 energy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Climate scientists have identified at least 16 tipping points in Earth's climate system. Once crossed, they trigger self-reinforcing changes. Five of these may already be at risk at current warming levels of 1.1C.
entries.hintEn: Save 15 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Research shows that consistent daily habits are more effective at reducing emissions than occasional large gestures. A daily 1 kg CO2 reduction adds up to 365 kg per year.
entries.hintEn: Maintain a 7-day streak to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The Keeling Curve, tracking atmospheric CO2 since 1958, shows an unbroken rise from 315 to over 420 parts per million. It remains one of the most important datasets in climate science.
entries.hintEn: Save 40 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Transportation accounts for about 16% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Shifting just 10% of car trips to cycling or public transport could reduce transport emissions by 4%.
entries.hintEn: Log 25 transport actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Ice and snow reflect up to 90% of sunlight back to space. As polar ice melts, darker ocean water absorbs more heat, creating a feedback loop that accelerates warming.
entries.hintEn: Save 100 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: If every commuter switched one car trip per week to public transit, it would reduce transport emissions by roughly 10%. Each bus replaces up to 40 cars during peak hours.
entries.hintEn: Complete the Green Transport Week challenge

entries.factEn: Arctic permafrost contains roughly 1.5 trillion tonnes of carbon, almost twice the amount currently in the atmosphere. Thawing permafrost could release vast quantities of methane and CO2.
entries.hintEn: Save 250 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The IEA's Net Zero by 2050 roadmap shows that reaching net zero is achievable but requires unprecedented transformation of how we produce and use energy, with no new fossil fuel projects approved after 2021.
entries.hintEn: Save 500 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Coastal ecosystems like mangroves, seagrasses, and salt marshes capture carbon up to 40 times faster per hectare than tropical forests, making them critical allies against climate change.
entries.hintEn: Log 3 water actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The ocean has absorbed about 30% of human-produced CO2, causing a 26% increase in acidity since pre-industrial times. This threatens shell-forming organisms from coral to plankton.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 water actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch covers an area roughly twice the size of Texas. It contains an estimated 80,000 tonnes of plastic, with most pieces smaller than 5 mm.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Coral reefs support 25% of all marine species but cover less than 1% of the ocean floor. Over half the world's coral reef cover has been lost since 1950 due to warming and acidification.
entries.hintEn: Log 25 water actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The ocean absorbs about 26% of all CO2 emissions, making it the planet's largest active carbon sink. Without this service, atmospheric CO2 levels would be roughly 50% higher.
entries.hintEn: Save 20 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Microplastics have been found in the deepest ocean trenches, atop Mount Everest, in human blood, and even in breast milk. An average person may ingest about 5 grams of plastic per week.
entries.hintEn: Log 30 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Every year, 8-12 million tonnes of plastic enter the ocean. Reducing single-use plastics at source is far more effective than cleanup, preventing 80% of marine plastic pollution.
entries.hintEn: Complete the Zero Waste Week challenge

entries.factEn: More than 80% of the ocean remains unmapped and unexplored. The deep sea may contain over 10 million undiscovered species, many of which could hold keys to new medicines.
entries.hintEn: Log 60 water actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Tides are among the most reliable natural cycles on Earth. Just as the moon consistently pulls the tides, consistent daily habits create a powerful rhythm of environmental impact.
entries.hintEn: Maintain a 14-day streak to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Over one-third of global fish stocks are overfished, and another 60% are at maximum capacity. Sustainable fishing practices could increase ocean food production by 16 million tonnes annually.
entries.hintEn: Log 100 water actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: A single great whale absorbs an average of 33 tonnes of CO2 over its lifetime. Before industrial whaling, whale populations removed hundreds of thousands of tonnes of carbon annually.
entries.hintEn: Log 200 water actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The global food system is responsible for about 26% of all greenhouse gas emissions, with animal products alone accounting for more than half of that total.
entries.hintEn: Log 3 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Roughly one-third of all food produced globally is wasted, about 1.3 billion tonnes annually. If food waste were a country, it would be the third-largest greenhouse gas emitter.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Healthy soil is the second-largest carbon sink after the ocean, storing about 2,500 billion tonnes of carbon. One teaspoon of soil contains more microorganisms than people on Earth.
entries.hintEn: Save 10 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Producing 1 kg of beef requires about 15,000 litres of water, compared to 1,250 for wheat and 287 for potatoes. Shifting diets can dramatically reduce water consumption.
entries.hintEn: Log 25 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: A plant-based diet reduces food-related emissions by up to 73% and uses 75% less land than a diet containing meat and dairy. Even small shifts like Meatless Mondays make a difference.
entries.hintEn: Complete the Vegan Week challenge

entries.factEn: Bees and other pollinators are responsible for one in every three bites of food we eat. Pollinator populations have declined by 40% in recent decades due to pesticides and habitat loss.
entries.hintEn: Log 50 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Composting food waste diverts methane from landfills and returns nutrients to soil. If all food waste in the US were composted, it would reduce emissions equivalent to 7.4 million cars.
entries.hintEn: Log 20 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Regenerative farming practices can capture up to 3 tonnes of CO2 per hectare per year while improving soil health, water retention, and biodiversity.
entries.hintEn: Log 80 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: If everyone went plant-based, global farmland use would drop by 75%, an area equivalent to the US, China, the EU, and Australia combined, allowing ecosystems to recover.
entries.hintEn: Complete the Veganuary challenge

entries.factEn: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway stores over 1.3 million seed samples from around the world, safeguarding crop diversity against natural disasters and climate change.
entries.hintEn: Log 150 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The global plant-based food market is projected to reach $162 billion by 2030. Every meal choice is a vote for the food system you want to see.
entries.hintEn: Log 365 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Every species on Earth is connected through intricate food webs. Removing even one species can trigger cascading effects throughout an entire ecosystem.
entries.hintEn: Log actions in 2 different categories

entries.factEn: Scientists estimate that the current rate of species extinction is 1,000 times higher than natural background rates. We are losing species at a pace not seen since the dinosaurs disappeared.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 total actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Wolves reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995 changed the course of rivers. By controlling elk populations, they allowed vegetation to recover, stabilizing riverbanks. This is called a trophic cascade.
entries.hintEn: Log actions in 4 different categories

entries.factEn: Forests are home to 80% of terrestrial biodiversity. The Amazon rainforest alone produces 6% of the world's oxygen and contains 10% of all species on Earth.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 4 different SDGs

entries.factEn: Scientists have identified about 8.7 million species on Earth, but estimates suggest 86% of land species and 91% of marine species remain undiscovered.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 different types of actions

entries.factEn: Wetlands cover only 6% of Earth's surface but store 35% of terrestrial carbon. They also filter water, prevent flooding, and support thousands of species.
entries.hintEn: Log actions in 6 different categories

entries.factEn: Underground fungal networks connect 90% of plant species, sharing nutrients and chemical warnings. A single network can span entire forests, earning the nickname 'Wood Wide Web.'
entries.hintEn: Log 75 total actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Keystone species have a disproportionately large effect on their ecosystems. Sea otters, for example, maintain kelp forests that absorb 12 times more CO2 per hectare than open ocean.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 8 different SDGs

entries.factEn: The variety of your actions mirrors the variety of life on Earth. Just as diverse ecosystems are more resilient, diverse sustainable habits create more lasting impact.
entries.hintEn: Log 25 different types of actions

entries.factEn: A healthy ecosystem needs producers, consumers, and decomposers working together. Similarly, sustainability needs action across all areas of life, from food to energy to community.
entries.hintEn: Log actions in all 9 categories

entries.factEn: Conservation works. Humpback whale populations have recovered from 10,000 to over 80,000 since the whaling ban. Giant pandas were downlisted from Endangered to Vulnerable in 2016.
entries.hintEn: Log 200 total actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Solar energy costs have fallen 89% since 2010, making it the cheapest source of electricity in history for most of the world. In 2023, solar generated over 5% of global electricity.
entries.hintEn: Log 3 energy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Cycling produces virtually zero emissions and is the most energy-efficient form of transport. If cycling's share of trips doubled globally, it would save 700 million tonnes of CO2 per year.
entries.hintEn: Log 5 transport actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Global wind power capacity doubled between 2017 and 2023. A single modern offshore wind turbine can power over 16,000 homes and displaces about 42,000 tonnes of CO2 per year.
entries.hintEn: Log 15 energy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Energy efficiency improvements since 2000 have avoided more CO2 emissions than all renewable energy combined. The cheapest and cleanest energy is the energy you don't use.
entries.hintEn: Save 8 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Public transit produces 45% less CO2 per passenger mile than single-occupancy cars. Walking and cycling produce essentially zero emissions while improving health.
entries.hintEn: Log 25 transport actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Smart grids can reduce peak energy demand by 15-20% through real-time monitoring and demand response. Shifting energy use to off-peak hours reduces reliance on fossil fuel backup plants.
entries.hintEn: Log 40 energy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Energy habits formed over 7-10 days tend to stick. Consistent small reductions in energy use, like turning off lights and unplugging chargers, save more over a year than one-off gestures.
entries.hintEn: Complete 10 daily challenges in a row

entries.factEn: Electric vehicles reached 18% of global car sales in 2023. EVs produce 50-70% fewer lifetime emissions than petrol cars, even accounting for battery production and electricity generation.
entries.hintEn: Log 60 transport actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: LED lighting uses 75% less energy than incandescent bulbs and lasts 25 times longer. If every household switched, it would be like removing 5 million cars from the road.
entries.hintEn: Save 150 kg of CO2 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Over 60% of the energy produced globally is wasted as heat, friction, or inefficiency. Closing this gap is one of the fastest and cheapest ways to reduce emissions.
entries.hintEn: Log 120 energy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Green hydrogen produced from renewable electricity could decarbonize 'hard to abate' sectors like steel, shipping, and aviation, potentially eliminating 6 billion tonnes of CO2 annually by 2050.
entries.hintEn: Log 200 energy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The world generates over 2 billion tonnes of solid waste annually, enough to fill 800,000 Olympic swimming pools. Only 13.5% is recycled and 5.5% composted.
entries.hintEn: Log 3 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The fashion industry produces 10% of global CO2 emissions and is the second-largest consumer of water. The average garment is worn only 7 times before being discarded.
entries.hintEn: Log 5 consumption actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: E-waste contains precious metals worth over $57 billion annually, but only 17.4% is formally recycled. One tonne of circuit boards contains more gold than 17 tonnes of gold ore.
entries.hintEn: Log 15 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The average smartphone is replaced every 2-3 years. Extending the life of electronics by just one year could save the equivalent CO2 of taking 2 million cars off the road annually in Europe alone.
entries.hintEn: Log 20 consumption actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Zero waste communities like Kamikatsu, Japan, sort waste into 45 categories and recycle 80% of their trash. The town aims to prove that zero waste living is achievable for everyone.
entries.hintEn: Complete the Zero Waste Week challenge

entries.factEn: Since 1950, humanity has produced 8.3 billion tonnes of plastic. Only 9% has been recycled, 12% incinerated, and 79% has accumulated in landfills or the natural environment.
entries.hintEn: Log 40 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Composting food scraps returns nutrients to soil and reduces methane from landfills. A household composting bin can divert over 100 kg of waste per year from landfill.
entries.hintEn: Log 15 food actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: A circular economy could generate $4.5 trillion in economic benefits by 2030. Unlike the linear 'take-make-waste' model, it designs out waste and keeps materials in use.
entries.hintEn: Maintain a 21-day streak to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Buying secondhand clothing saves about 13 kg of CO2 per garment compared to buying new. The resale market is growing 25 times faster than the overall retail market.
entries.hintEn: Log 60 consumption actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: In a fully circular economy, waste becomes food for new products. Companies like Interface have shown that 'Mission Zero' manufacturing is commercially viable and more profitable.
entries.hintEn: Log 100 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The zero waste movement proves that individual choices scale. When Bea Johnson's family of four produced only one jar of waste per year, it inspired a global movement.
entries.hintEn: Log 250 recycling actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The 17 Sustainable Development Goals were adopted by all 193 UN member states in 2015. They represent a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 3 different SDGs

entries.factEn: Community-led sustainability initiatives consistently outperform top-down programs by leveraging local knowledge, stronger participation, and social trust. Local action creates ripple effects that inspire neighbors, businesses, and policymakers.
entries.hintEn: Log 5 community actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: The richest 10% of the global population produce 50% of emissions, while the poorest 50% produce only 12%. Climate change disproportionately impacts those least responsible for it.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 5 different SDGs

entries.factEn: Young people under 25 make up 42% of the global population and will live with the consequences of today's climate decisions the longest. Youth movements have already shifted policy worldwide.
entries.hintEn: Log 10 advocacy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Indigenous peoples protect 80% of the world's remaining biodiversity. Lands managed by indigenous communities have equal or lower deforestation rates than government-protected areas.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 7 different SDGs

entries.factEn: Research shows that when one person in a neighborhood installs solar panels, their neighbors are significantly more likely to follow. One study found adoption probability is 89% higher among people who know a solar panel owner.
entries.hintEn: Log 25 community actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Research shows that sustained civic engagement is significantly more effective at driving environmental policy change than one-time actions. Consistent participation builds relationships, expertise, and political momentum that isolated efforts cannot match.
entries.hintEn: Complete 14 daily challenges in a row

entries.factEn: 2.2 billion people still lack safely managed drinking water. Yet water-efficient technologies could reduce global water demand by 30% while improving access for those who need it most.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 10 different SDGs

entries.factEn: Environmental advocacy has driven every major green policy from the Clean Air Act to the Paris Agreement. Individual voices, amplified together, create the political will for systemic change.
entries.hintEn: Log 40 advocacy actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Scientists have identified 9 planetary boundaries that define a 'safe operating space' for humanity. Six of the nine have already been crossed, signaling increased risk of destabilizing Earth systems.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 13 different SDGs

entries.factEn: The Montreal Protocol, which phased out ozone-depleting substances, is the most successful environmental treaty in history. It proves that global cooperation can solve planetary-scale problems.
entries.hintEn: Log actions for 15 different SDGs

entries.factEn: Every journey begins with a single step. The hardest part of building a new habit is starting. You've already taken yours.
entries.hintEn: Maintain a 3-day streak to discover this entry

entries.factEn: People who set specific goals are 42% more likely to achieve them. Daily challenges turn vague intentions into concrete actions.
entries.hintEn: Complete 3 daily challenges in a row

entries.factEn: You've reached level 5! Research shows it takes about 66 days to form a new habit. Every level up brings you closer to making sustainability second nature.
entries.hintEn: Reach level 5 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: After 7 consecutive days, a behavior starts wiring itself into your basal ganglia (the habit center of your brain), transitioning from conscious effort to automatic routine.
entries.hintEn: Maintain a 7-day streak to discover this entry

entries.factEn: People who actively seek out new information are more likely to change their behavior. You've been reading and learning. Knowledge is the foundation of meaningful action.
entries.hintEn: View 14 daily eco-facts to discover this entry

entries.factEn: A full week of completed challenges shows real commitment. Consistency in small actions creates a compound effect on your environmental impact.
entries.hintEn: Complete 7 daily challenges in a row

entries.factEn: At level 15, your cumulative CO2 savings are making a real difference. If 1,000 people did what you're doing, the collective impact would equal planting a small forest.
entries.hintEn: Reach level 15 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: You've read 50 eco-facts! Studies show that environmental knowledge correlates strongly with pro-environmental behavior. You're building the understanding that drives lasting change.
entries.hintEn: View 50 daily eco-facts to discover this entry

entries.factEn: 30 consecutive days of action is remarkable. You've proven that sustainability isn't a phase; it's part of who you are. Habits this strong tend to last for years.
entries.hintEn: Maintain a 30-day streak to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Completing a 30-day challenge requires discipline, planning, and genuine commitment. You didn't just try. You followed through.
entries.hintEn: Complete the Monthly Momentum challenge

entries.factEn: Level 30 puts you in the top tier of Seed users. Your sustained effort represents hundreds of real-world actions and a significant reduction in your carbon footprint.
entries.hintEn: Reach level 30 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Level 50 is legendary. The cumulative impact of your actions is equivalent to planting dozens of trees. You're not just building habits; you're building a legacy.
entries.hintEn: Reach level 50 to discover this entry

entries.factEn: People who publicly identify as environmentally conscious are 30% more likely to maintain sustainable behaviors. Your profile is your commitment made visible.
entries.hintEn: Complete your profile to discover this entry

entries.factEn: Sustainability is most powerful when it spans multiple areas of life. Acting across three categories shows you're thinking holistically about your impact.
entries.hintEn: Log actions in 3 different categories

entries.factEn: Trying different actions helps you find what works for your lifestyle. The most sustainable habits are the ones that fit naturally into your daily routine.
entries.hintEn: Try 5 different types of actions

entries.factEn: 10 challenges completed! Each one was a small experiment in living more sustainably. You're building a toolkit of habits that will serve you for life.
entries.hintEn: Complete 10 total challenges

entries.factEn: You've discovered 25 Eco-Dex entries! Each one represents a piece of the sustainability puzzle. Together, they paint a picture of how interconnected our world really is.
entries.hintEn: Discover 25 Eco-Dex entries

entries.factEn: With 15 different action types tried, you've moved beyond the basics. You're exploring the full range of ways to reduce your environmental impact.
entries.hintEn: Try 15 different types of actions

entries.factEn: Learning is its own form of activism. By deepening your understanding, you become better equipped to make informed choices and inspire others.
entries.hintEn: Log 15 learning actions to discover this entry

entries.factEn: 50 challenges completed! You've made daily sustainability challenges a genuine part of your routine. That kind of consistency is rare and powerful.
entries.hintEn: Complete 50 total challenges

entries.factEn: You've discovered half of all Eco-Dex entries! You're well on your way to becoming a true sustainability encyclopedia. Keep exploring.
entries.hintEn: Discover 50 Eco-Dex entries

entries.factEn: 30 different action types! You've tried nearly everything Seed has to offer. Your breadth of experience makes you a walking guide to sustainable living.
entries.hintEn: Try 30 different types of actions

entries.factEn: 90 Eco-Dex entries discovered! You can almost see the finish line. The last few entries are the rarest. Only the most dedicated explorers complete the full collection.
